questions.question: How do you handle an interview question you don't know?
questions.title: Handling Unknown Questions
questions.direct_answer: When you don't know an answer, don't fake it — say 'I'm not certain, but here's how I'd find out', then reason from what you DO know. Interviewers test honesty and problem-solving, not memorization; a confident 'I don't know, but I'd check the docs / write a test / ask a senior' beats a wrong guess. If it's a coding question, talk through what you'd try (edge cases, a simpler version, the docs). The trap to avoid is freezing, guessing wrong and confidently, or pretending you know — all signal worse than an honest 'I'd look it up'.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Freezing, or guessing confidently and wrong — both worse than an honest 'I'd look it up'.
